concerns.text: The plan simulates `review_effort_duration` for LLM‑generated PRs by sampling from a KDE built on human PRs (see lines describing the five‑step simulation). Because the primary outcome is never actually observed for the synthetic cohort, any observed difference after matching cannot be attributed to the LLM generation itself; the analysis merely reflects the imputed distribution. This breaks causal validity and makes the central hypothesis (LLM code leads to longer review effort) untestable.

Relatedly, the construct validity of the primary outcome is compromised: `review_effort_duration` is defined as a real timestamp for human PRs but as a simulated value for LLM PRs. Treating a simulated metric as equivalent to a measured one violates the requirement that the measurement truly reflect the construct of reviewer effort, rendering the statistical test results uninterpretable.
